From the journal

Twelve routes worth the drive

October is the month the crowds thin out and the light goes gold by four. We asked the shop staff for the routes they keep coming back to, and the answers ran from a two-hour ridge loop to a three-day hut traverse. A few rules first: start early, carry a head torch even if you plan to be down by lunch, and tell someone where you are going.

„Der Weg ist das Ziel“, sagte der Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaftskapitän, und das gilt besonders im Herbst.

The full list is on our journal, with GPX files for each. Look for the new hut on route nine, and pack micro­spikes for anything above 1,800 m after mid-month. Our team in Kyoto added one too: 紅葉の季節は早朝が一番静かです。 Go early.

Field notes

A proper way to dry wet boots

Pull the insoles, stuff with newspaper, change it every few hours, and keep them well away from the radiator. Leather cracks; glue lets go. Patience is cheaper than a new pair. 🥾 👩‍👩‍👧‍👦 👍🏽 🏳️‍🌈 café́ naïve

Map: https://maps.example/?q=47.3769,8.5417&layers=terrain,huts,water&zoom=13&share=ZXhhbXBsZS1yb3V0ZS1uaW5lLXRoZS1sb25nLW9uZQ

Before you go

The October checklist
01 Check the forecast twice: the night before and at the trailhead.
02 Pack a warm layer you think you won't need.
03 Charge the head torch, then pack the spare batteries anyway.
  • Map and compass, even with a phone
  • 1 litre of water per three hours
  • Emergency blanket
